sentences.text: IN  S.B. Criminal Appeal No.102/2023

Bhagwan Singh Son Of Kishan Lal, Aged About 23 Years,
Resident Of Banskhedi Lodhan Police Station Bhalta District Jhalawar (Raj) (At Present In District Jail Jhalawar)
 ----Appellant  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through PP  ----Respondent
For Appellant(s) : Mr. Ali Mohammed Khan
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Amit Punia, PP  Mr. Rohit Khandelwal, for complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR UPMAN  Order 08/10/2024 1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant-appellant, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant on the application for suspension of execution of sentence.
Perused the material available on record.

2. The applicant-appellant herein has been convicted for offence under Sections 363, 366 & 376(3)
of IPC and Section 5(l)/6 of POCSO Act, 2012 vide judgment dated 02.09.2022 passed by learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, 2012 and Commission for Protection of Children Rights Act, 2005, No.1,
Jhalawar in Sessions Case No.38/2020 (CIS No.38/2020) and has been sentenced to maximum punishment of 20 years.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that learned trial court has erred in convicting and sentencing the applicant as mentioned above.

sentences.text: Learned trial court has not appreciated the evidence in right and correct perspective.
He further submits that in FIR itself, age of the victim has been mentioned as 19 years.
Her age mentioned in the school record is not conclusive as at the time of admission, no supporting document was produced which is admitted by PW-1 (Principal).
He further submits that medical evidence available on record suggests that victim was fully grown up girl as at the time of medical examination, her height was 162 cm and weight was 46 kg.

It is further submitted that victim was a consenting party as she left her parental home on her own and travelled with the appellant in the public conveyance and during this period, she did not make any complaint.
It has also been admitted by the victim that she travelled with the appellant in bus.
Despite having several opportunities, no complaint was made by victim.
She remained in the company of the appellant for about two and half months.
He further submits that appellant was also aged about 23 years at the time of alleged incident.
It is further submitted that appellant has suffered incarceration of almost five years till date.
There is no immediate prospect of this appeal being heard and disposed of in near future and hearing of the appeal will take time.
4. Learned Public Prosecutor assisted by learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposes the submissions made by the learned counsel for appellant.

They submit that as per school record,
victim was aged about 15 years at the time of alleged [2024:RJ-JP:42333] (3 of 4) [SOSA-132/2023]
incident.
It is further submitted that victim/complainant has duly been informed about hearing of this appeal.

5. Upon a consideration of the arguments advanced on behalf of the appellant and having regard to the facts and circumstances as available on the record especially the fact that age of the victim has been mentioned as 19 years in the FIR; considering the physical features as height and weight of the victim as mentioned in the school record as also period of incarceration suffered by appellant, but without making any comment on the merits/demerits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for suspending the sentences awarded to the accused appellant during pendency of the instant appeal.

6. Accordingly, the application for suspension of sentence filed under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the sentences passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, 2012 and Commission for Protection of Children Rights Act, 2005, No.1, Jhalawar vide judgment dated 02.09.2022 in Sessions Case No.38/2020 (CIS No.38/2020) against the appellant-applicant Bhagwan Singh Son Of Kishan Lal, shall remain suspended till final disposal of the aforesaid appeal and he shall be released on bail, provided he executes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance in this court on 08.11.2024 and whenever ordered to do so till the disposal of the appeal on the conditions indicated below:-
1.
